page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core architecture within the Edsv6 family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, the instance provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It integrates a massive memory array of 768.0 GB of RAM alongside 5,670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for hardware-accelerated matrix operations and vector compute.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput across core computational and memory-bound workloads. The system achieves high memory read bandwidth, reaching 3,723.24 GB/sec on cached 16 KB blocks and 234.94 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks, complementing a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 306.68 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks show solid execution density with a PassMark CPU score of 63,798.65 and Geekbench multi-core score of 18,862.0. Database operation benchmarks reach 24,034.71, supported by Redis SET operations processing 67.4 million transactions per second. In addition, hardware-accelerated matrix extensions allow solid LLM prompt processing throughput despite the absence of a dedicated GPU.

By offering 16 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance delivers high memory density on a 48-vCPU allocation, optimizing per-core software licensing costs for memory-hungry services. With substantial high-speed local NVMe storage and dedicated processing threads, the configuration fits large relational database systems, in-memory caches, distributed analytics engines, and intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 family featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs on 24 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores clocked at 4.2 GHz. Providing an expansive 768.0 GB of memory (16.0 GB per vCPU) and 5,670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, it pairs high-capacity RAM with fast local I/O. The hardware platform includes AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions, driving strong memory bandwidth up to 3,723.24 GB/sec cached and high transaction processing rates of 67.4 million Redis SET operations per second. PassMark database tests achieve 24,034.71 points, confirming rapid execution for data-intensive processing. The constrained core configuration allows organizations to maintain massive memory allocations while optimizing core-based software licensing costs, making it well fitted for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, and heavy ETL pipelines.
